overall: The AG found no violation on the alleged notice-specificity and March 31 agenda claims, but noted unalleged remote-participation and roll-call lapses and reminded the Board of its duties.

allegations.summary: Notices for March 17, 24, April 5 and 7 listed only 'Selectmen discuss FY22 Budget' but allegedly should have named specific department budgets.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the notices for these four meetings were sufficiently specific because they informed the public that the Board would be generally reviewing the budget for the upcoming fiscal year and reflected the actual discussions held during the meetings.

allegations.summary: Notice for the April 6 meeting was alleged to be insufficiently detailed, but the Board did not meet on April 6 and discussed no budget.
allegations.key_passage: Where a public body does not actually engage in any deliberation on a particular topic, it cannot violate the Open Meeting Law with respect to the sufficiency of the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Budget was discussed on March 31 under the 'Any Other Business' notice item, which listed no budget topic, allegedly improperly.
allegations.key_passage: A public body may discuss a topic not listed on a meeting notice if the topic was not anticipated by the chair 48 hours in advance of the meeting.

allegations.summary: Not alleged. AG noted the chair did not announce names of the three members participating remotely at the start of five remote meetings.
allegations.key_passage: However, the chair of the Board did not announce the names of the three members who were participating remotely at the beginning of the meetings.

allegations.summary: Not alleged. AG noted votes at five remote meetings were not taken by roll call, as the remote-participation rules require.
allegations.key_passage: In addition, votes taken during these five meetings were not conducted by roll call vote.
